subject: Private deployment DPA + BYOK & operator access — clarifications requested
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@medisyshealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medisyshealth.com, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@medisyshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifications on private deploy DPA and BYOK flow

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the DPA draft you sent yesterday. A couple of things came up in procurement/legal while we were reviewing private deployment (VPC/on-prem) options:

- We need a clear statement of operator access windows (who can access customer environments and under what trigger).
- Please confirm the key custody model for BYOK: will Redwood ever have access to unwrapped customer keys, or is the keystore agent strictly customer-controlled?
- For cross-border support, what information will be in logs sent back to Redwood (if any)? We need to narrow PII fields that are allowed in telemetry.

Can you point us to the appendix that shows the BYOK key handshake and any proposed break-glass protocol? Also, procurement would like to request a short matrix that maps subprocessor types to the data categories they may see.

We are under a tight timeline — aiming to finish legal review by 11/27. Happy to schedule a 30-minute call if that helps.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Sr. Contracts Manager
Medisys Health

--
attachments: none referenced in this message

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifications on private deploy DPA and BYOK flow

Samantha —

Appreciate the quick review and clear asks. I attached an updated DPA (redwood-dpa-draft-v2.docx) and a BYOK diagram (byok_keyflow-diagram.png) that should address most items. Quick summary of our positions:

1) Operator access: Redwood requires on-call operator access for emergency remediation (e.g., kernel panic, hardware failover). Access is strictly role-based and time-limited; we propose a documented approval flow (customer ticket -> designated admin approval -> short-lived session). We have an "operator-access-appendix.pdf" that defines SLAs and the audit trail.

2) BYOK custody: For private deployments, the keystore agent runs in your VPC/on-prem tenant. Redwood never receives your plaintext/unwrapped key material. We only receive a key handle (opaque identifier) for routing. The agent performs local unwrap/wrap operations; we can add stronger language if your security team wants absolute proof (e.g., attestation tokens from the agent).

3) Telemetry and logs: By default we send only non-PII service telemetry (latency, error codes, model variant). Any telemetry that could contain redacted prompt/response snippets is opt-in and can be configured to never leave your VPC. The DPA shows a table of allowable fields.

I'm looping Laura for legal language edits and Marissa on operational controls. If you'd like, we can do a focused call Thursday 11/25 at 10am PT to walk through the appendix and the break-glass flow.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dpa-draft-v2.docx, byok_keyflow-diagram.png

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@medisyshealth.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifications on private deploy DPA and BYOK flow

Hi Samantha, Karthik —

Thanks for the clear list. A few notes from legal on the attached DPA v2:

- We edited the BYOK clause to state: "Customer retains sole possession and control of Key Material. Redwood is prohibited from intentionally accessing plaintext Key Material except under explicit, customer-approved attestation scenarios."
- Operator access: we propose adding a Section 7.3 requiring customer-specified admin identities and an API-based approval token for any operator session. That token must be logged to the customer's audit endpoint in real time.
- Subprocessors: we added a matrix (Table B) that enumerates classes (GPU infra, storage, monitoring) and the minimal data each class requires. This table is intentionally conservative; if Medisys needs further carve-outs we can mark them as restricted.
- Break-glass: legal wants a maximum three-person internal Redwood escalation for emergency access, with forensic export delivered to customer and a written post-incident report within 7 days.

I left a couple of redlines where we need confirmation from Medisys (noted inline). If you can confirm the admin identities and whether you accept attestation tokens, we can finalize.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: operator-access-appendix.pdf

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@medisyshealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifications on private deploy DPA and BYOK flow

Samantha / team —

Operational note from our side: our break-glass prototype uses an HSM-backed attestation flow where the keystore agent emits an ephemeral signed confirmation that it performed the unwrap locally. We will provide sample attestation tokens you can validate.

On operator sessions: I propose the following hard constraints to put in the appendix and SLA:
- Access window = single-use session tokens, max 30 minutes per session.
- Session initiation requires 2 approvals (customer admin + Redwood on-call lead).
- All session keystrokes are recorded and delivered to the customer's secure audit collector within 1 hour.

If Medisys needs air-gapped/exclusive on-prem support (no outbound telemetry at all), we can offer an on-prem bundle that removes egress endpoints but adds a dedicated support engineer rotation (costed separately).

Happy to demo the attestation sequence on Thursday if that works.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@medisyshealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifications on private deploy DPA and BYOK flow

Laura / Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed edits. Procurement and InfoSec reviewed the attachments this morning. A few quick confirmations:

- We accept the BYOK language as drafted; InfoSec will validate the sample attestation tokens during a tech review.
- Operator session constraints look reasonable — procurement wants the 2-approver flow documented in the SOW.
- For telemetry, Medisys will opt out of prompt/response snippets and require that any telemetry containing metadata be filtered to remove user identifiers.

We'd like to schedule the 30-minute technical run-through Thursday 11/25 at 10am PT (we are available). Please send the calendar invite and dial-in. Assuming the tech review goes well, procurement will circulate the DPA redline by 11/27 as requested.

Best,
Daniel Cho
Senior Security Engineer
Medisys Health

--
